options.label: COBRA (keep your old plan)
options.availabilityReason: Available if your employer had 20 or more employees.
notes: Same plan, doctors and drug coverage you had before. Lasts up to 18 months.

options.label: Marketplace plan (HealthCare.gov)
options.availabilityReason: You can enroll because you lost job-based coverage.
notes: Deductible starts over at $0 on a new plan.

subsidy.reason: an affordable spouse or partner plan is available

options.label: Medicaid / CHIP
options.availabilityReason: Children often qualify for CHIP at this income, depending on your state's limit.
notes: Medicaid and CHIP look at your current monthly income. You can apply any time.
Likely only for the children in your household. The adults would need another option.
Usually no premium and very low costs when you get care. Some states charge small CHIP premiums.

members.reason: Income is above your state's Medicaid limit for adults.
Income is above your state's Medicaid limit for adults.
Children often qualify for CHIP at this income, depending on your state's limit.

options.label: Spouse's or partner's employer plan
options.availabilityReason: Losing your coverage lets you join their plan outside open enrollment.
notes: New plan, so the deductible starts over at $0. Check that your doctors are in its network.
We used typical employer-plan deductible and out-of-pocket amounts for the missing ones.

timeline.label: Your old coverage ends
timeline.detail: The last day your old plan covers you.

timeline.label: Join a spouse's or partner's employer plan
timeline.detail: Employer plans must give at least 30 days after you lose coverage. Ask their HR; some plans allow longer.

timeline.label: Earliest Marketplace coverage start
timeline.detail: Coverage starts the 1st of the month after you pick a plan.

timeline.label: COBRA election notice should arrive by
timeline.detail: Your employer has 30 days to tell the plan, and the plan has 14 more to notify you. If it hasn't arrived by then, contact HR or the plan administrator.

timeline.label: Marketplace special enrollment window
timeline.detail: You can pick a Marketplace plan from 60 days before to 60 days after your coverage ends.

timeline.label: Open enrollment for 2027 coverage
timeline.detail: HealthCare.gov dates. If your state runs its own exchange, its dates may differ.

timeline.label: Last day to elect COBRA
timeline.detail: 60 days after the notice arrives (or after coverage ends, if later). This date is an estimate until you have the notice.

timeline.label: Latest first COBRA payment
timeline.detail: Due 45 days after the day you elect. This is the latest date, if you elect on the last day. The first payment covers every month back to when coverage ended.

timeline.label: COBRA would end (maximum 18 months)
timeline.detail: When COBRA runs out, you get a new window to enroll in a Marketplace plan.

timeline.label: Medicaid / CHIP: apply any time
timeline.detail: There's no enrollment window. Coverage can start right away, and sometimes it's backdated up to 3 months.

watchOuts.title: Dropping COBRA later won't open a Marketplace window
watchOuts.body: If you choose COBRA and later cancel it or stop paying, you can't switch to a Marketplace plan until open enrollment. Running out of COBRA's full term does open a new window. If a Marketplace plan might be better, decide before your window closes on Nov 29, 2026.

watchOuts.title: The spouse or partner plan blocks Marketplace subsidies
watchOuts.body: Family coverage costs $780 a month. That's at or below 9.96% of household income, which counts as "affordable." Family members who are offered that plan can't get Marketplace subsidies.

watchOuts.title: The window to join a spouse's or partner's plan is short
watchOuts.body: It's usually only 30 days after your coverage ends. Ask their HR right away.

watchOuts.title: Sample plan data
watchOuts.body: The Marketplace plans shown are sample data for testing, not real prices.

watchOuts.title: Your children may qualify even if you don't
watchOuts.body: Children often qualify for Medicaid or CHIP at higher incomes than adults. Families sometimes put children on CHIP and adults on another plan, which can lower total cost.

watchOuts.title: COBRA keeps what you've already paid toward your deductible
watchOuts.body: You've met $1,200 of your deductible this year. COBRA keeps that progress. A Marketplace or spouse's plan starts over at zero.

watchOuts.title: Only 3 months left in the plan year
watchOuts.body: Deductibles on every plan reset January 1, so the advantage of keeping COBRA's deductible progress is short-lived. Plan for open enrollment too.

watchOuts.title: Severance and unemployment count as income
watchOuts.body: Both count when the Marketplace and Medicaid look at your income.

watchOuts.title: COBRA depends on employer size
watchOuts.body: Federal COBRA covers employers with 20 or more employees. If yours was smaller, your state's "mini-COBRA" law may apply instead. Check your notice.

nextSteps.title: Apply for Medicaid or CHIP
nextSteps.body: Apply any time. One application on HealthCare.gov checks Medicaid, CHIP and subsidies together. You can also apply directly with your state Medicaid office.

nextSteps.title: Ask your spouse's or partner's HR about adding your family
nextSteps.body: Losing your coverage lets you join their plan outside open enrollment. Ask for the monthly cost and request enrollment before the deadline.

nextSteps.title: Compare plans and enroll on HealthCare.gov
nextSteps.body: Choose "lost job-based coverage" as your reason. Pick a plan by the day your coverage ends to avoid a gap.

nextSteps.title: Decide whether to elect COBRA
nextSteps.body: Use the election form in your COBRA notice. Coverage is backdated to when your plan ended, so you can wait to decide, but not past the deadline.

nextSteps.title: If you elect COBRA, make the first payment
nextSteps.body: Due 45 days after you elect. It covers every month back to when your old coverage ended.

nextSteps.title: Keep proof of your coverage loss
nextSteps.body: Save your termination letter, COBRA notice, or a letter from the plan showing the end date. The Marketplace or a spouse's plan may ask for it.

nextSteps.title: Report income changes after you enroll
nextSteps.body: If you get a new job or your income changes, update HealthCare.gov right away to avoid repaying subsidies.
